# `\textcolor{pmxgreen}{(pmxhelpr)}`{=latex} Function Friday
:::

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source(here::here("R", "setup.R"))
```

The dose-proportionality assessment toolchain  within `pmxhelpr`
consists of a summary function, `df_doseprop()`, and a dual-mode plotting 
function, `plot_doseprop()`, mirroring the VPC approach.

Dose proportionality assessment evaluates whether exposure increases 
proportionally with dose. The standard approach to this assessment is power law 
regression based on the relationship:

$$Exposure = \alpha \cdot DOSE^\gamma$$

which is estimated via linear regression after log transformation as:

$$\ln(Exposure) = ln(\alpha) + \gamma \cdot \ln(DOSE)$$

This assessment is typically performed using single dose Cmax and AUC to 
assess which phase of the PK profile is contributing most to non-linearity
(e.g., absorption rate [Ka], absorption extent [F], or elimination [CL]). 

Interpretation is generally based on comparison of the confidence interval 
of the power estimate ($\gamma$) to the value indicating dose-proportionality
($\gamma = 1$). the:

  + CI includes 1: dose-proportional
  + CI excludes 1, contained below 1: less than dose-proportional
  + CI excludes 1, contained above 1: greater than dose-proportional

The `data_sad_nca` dataset internal to `pmxhelpr` will be used in this example,
which contains NCA parameters for a virtual SAD and FE study. This example will
filter to the SAD part to exclude the potential impact of food.

```{r data-prep}
data_nca1 <- filter(data_sad_nca, PART == "Part 1-SAD")
```

# Dose-proportionality Assessment Tabulation: `df_doseprop()`

The `df_doseprop()` function performs the log-log regression of exposure 
metrics vs dose and returns a summary object. 

There are two required arguments:

  + `data` — a `data.frame` of NCA parameters
  + `metrics` — a character vector of exposure metric names in `data`

{{< pagebreak >}}
  
And three optional arguments involed which must be specified if different 
from the default values:

  + `metric_name_var`: variable in `data` containing metric names requested in
      `metrics`, default `PPTESTCD`.
  + `metric_value_var`: variable in `data` containing exposure metric values, 
      default `PPORRES`
  + `dose_var`: variable in `data` containg the numeric dose amount, 
      default `DOSE`.
      
```{r df-doseprop-obj}
dose_prop_obj <- df_doseprop(data_nca1, metrics = c("aucinf.obs", "cmax"))
dose_prop_obj
```

The returned `doseprop_stats` S3 class object provides a print summary of
the `stats` data.frame with dimension and configuration information. 

```{r table-defaults}
dose_prop_obj$stats %>% select(-Intercept, -StandardError) %>% gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Dose-proportionality Assessment (Part 1-SAD)") %>%
  tab_options(latex.use_longtable = TRUE,table.font.size = px(10),
          heading.title.font.size = px(14), heading.subtitle.font.size = px(14))
```
  
{{< pagebreak >}}

# Plotting with `plot_doseprop()`

`plot_doseprop()` is the dual mode plotting function, which can plot a 
pre-computed `doseprop_stats` output from `df_doseprop` or perform one-shot 
log-log regression statistic computation and plotting. 

The output is a `ggplot`object with one panel per metric, where the facet label 
includes the metric name and the `PowerCI` text. The plot axis limits are 
rounded to the nearest half log units by default.

```{r plot-pcvpc-cont-log, fig.height=4, fig.width=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
plot_doseprop(dose_prop_obj)
```

The required arguments in the one-step pathway are the same as `df_doseprop()`. 
Additional arguments to `df_doseprop()`, which can were not detailed previously, 
control options within the log-log regression.

  + `method`: distribution used to calculate the confidence interval. Default 
  is `"normal"`. Alternative `"tdist"` may be preferred for small samples size 
    where normality cannot be assumed.
  + `ci`: confidence interval to return expressed as a proportion. Default is 
    `"0.9"` based on the 90% CI used in bioequivalence assessment.
  + `sigdigits`: number of significant digits to return in outputs
